images.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset: disclosed StackRank Dogs field-guide illustration. Generate one original 1536×1024 landscape portrait of one mature adult Mountain Cur, exact catalog VBO:0200914. Text-only generation; no image inputs. Independently researched morphology: A mature medium-sized powerful, agile Mountain Cur in hard muscular condition, square to slightly longer than tall, long functional legs. Flat broad skull, moderate stop, muzzle slightly shorter than skull with strong underjaw and tight lips, brown eyes, black square nose. High-set short-to-medium broad-based drop ears. Strong moderately long slightly arched neck, broad level back, muscular loin, deep chest to elbows, slight tuck-up. Strong straight forelegs, balanced muscular hindquarters, well-bent stifles and low hocks, compact moderately oval arched paws. Short close dense smooth coat with soft undercoat; choose warm yellow-buckskin with a small white breast fleck. Low-set complete natural medium-length straight tapered tail, gently elevated, neither curled nor docked; UKC general appearance and tail sections establish this form, and its full-tail clause accepts the natural option. Show a relaxed dog-eye-level three-quarter standing pose facing left, head turned gently toward the viewer. All four coherent paws planted visibly on firm ground, natural limb courses and joints, believable weight and contact shadows. Frame entire head, ears, body, four legs and paws, and complete attached natural tail with generous crop-safe space. Keep the free tail tip clearly separate from hind legs. Setting: A firm, open sandstone-and-earth clearing beside Appalachian deciduous woodland, a few dry leaves clear of the paws, soft late-afternoon light. Photorealistic restrained earth tones, natural short coat detail, softly separated background. Create a fresh individual, markings, pose and camera arrangement. No source show stage, handler, trophy, rosette or prize board. No collar, leash, people, other animals, buildings, vehicles, prey, text, logos, watermark, extra limbs or malformed paws. Do not recreate a researched photograph or named championship dog.

profileEvidence.summary: Keen to work with its handler, the Mountain Cur brings strong treeing instincts and persistence to a hunt. It often follows a trail with its head raised, circling an older scent until a fresher trail appears; its voice may range from silent to freely barking. Rural American breeders preserved it for squirrel, raccoon and larger game.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: A persistent tree dog that tends to hunt with its head raised, circling older scent to find a fresher trail.
